newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Three die but two survive W.Samoa plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Three die but two survive W.Samoa plane crash.

text.p: Three people died but two survivors were plucked from the wreckage of a Twin Otter aircraft which crashed in the South Pacific nation of Western Samoa on Wednesday, the airline's managing director said.
Richard Gates, managing director of Polynesian Airlines, said the remaining three people on flight PH211 were dead.

"There were two operating crew and three passengers, and it would appear that there are two survivors," Gates told Reuters. The airline had earlier said it feared all five people aboard had been killed.

Gates said the plane had crashed into a hillside near Moamoa, about six kilometres (four miles) south of the Western Samoan capital Apia, at about 11 a.m. (2200 GMT). It was flying to Apia from Pago Pago in American Samoa.
The cause of the accident had not yet been determined but Gates said strong winds and heavy rain were buffeting the region at the time of the crash.
"The weather is marginal...(but) certainly the weather conditions are not unusual for this time of year," he said.
The airline had asked New Zealand authorities to undertake an investigation into the accident.
Polynesian Airlines is Western Samoa's national carrier and has a fleet of four aircraft.
